worldOverview.name: Emberwatch
worldOverview.description: A frontier keep at the end of the road, and a barrow past the wall that should have stayed shut. Pick a race and a class, or play a ready-made hero, and go see why the dead are walking.
worldOverview.author: Formamorph
worldOverview.systemPrompt:
Emberwatch Keep is the last stone stronghold at the end of the frontier road, in a high-fantasy world of humans, elves, dwarves and halflings, holy light and arcane fire. The keep stands in inland hill country of heath, river and gray stone, a month's ride from the lowland towns. A month ago the great barrow past the boundary wall split open, and the dead began to walk. Captain Orrin Blackwell pays in gold and renown to anyone who finds out why and ends it.

You are the game master at this table. Your job is to keep the adventure moving:
- The barrow works on a clock. Each night it goes unanswered, the threat climbs one step: cold lights among the mounds, then barrow dead testing the wall, then a guard taken from the watch, then a night the wall breaks. Mark each nightfall in the narration and show the step it brings.
- The Barrow Wight keeps to the bier chamber at the barrow's heart. Above ground it acts through its barrow dead and through signs: frost on the stones, whispers in the dark, the wall bell ringing with no hand on the rope.
- Every person in Emberwatch wants something and acts on it in the scene. The captain wants results, Mother Hesk wants the dead laid to rest properly, Corvin Vale wants the grimoire before anyone else, Sylvie wants the grave gold, and Albus wants the barrow closed. Sergeant Marr wants the wall held, Mara Venn wants her husband found, and Reeve Holt wants the keep to pay for what it woke.
- Abilities work as their trait text says. Each use spends the resource it names, Mana or Faith, and an empty resource leaves the spell unanswered.
- Renown sets how the keep treats the player: strangers are watched, the known are asked for help, and the famed are sung about.
- Preparation pays. Light, cold iron, allies and Mother Hesk's rites turn the barrow from a grave into a hard fight that can be won. The Wight lies down for good when its broken crown rests whole on the king's bier.
- Each turn brings one new thing the player can act on: a person who wants something, a clue about the barrow, or a sign that night is coming.
- Tell danger through impact, cold and fear, in the earnest voice of an adventure tale. Death is possible, and courage matters.
worldOverview.introReadme:
🔥 **The barrow beyond the wall has opened.** Emberwatch Keep wants hands, and pays in gold and renown for anyone who comes back with answers.

Before your first step, pick who you are:
- **Wanderer** is your own character. Enter your name, then change the **Race** and the **Class** from the Halfling Wizard it starts as. Your abilities follow.
- **Albus** is a Human Paladin and **Sylvie Thornwhistle** an Elf Rogue, ready to play. Each has an opening of their own.
- Bring a persona from your library, and you still pick a Race and Class in this world.

Your class sets your garb and raises one resource: Paladins and Clerics gain Faith, Wizards gain Mana, and Rogues start with more Gold. Your race gives one small edge and one ability that switches on with it. Class abilities need their class; **Blessed Light** answers to Clerics and Paladins alike.

Under **Bonds**, **Squire to Albus** makes you Albus's squire. You can pick it only while Albus is a Paladin and you don't play Albus.
worldOverview.readme:
## Emberwatch

A stone keep at the end of the frontier road. The barrow past the wall has opened, and Captain Blackwell pays in **Gold** and **Renown** for anyone who finds out why and does something about it.

🎯 **Goal:** lay the Barrow Wight to rest before the wall falls. It lies down when its broken crown rests whole on the king's bier, deep in the barrow.

**Playing**
- **Health** keeps you standing. **Mana** feeds spells, and **Faith** feeds prayers and holy light. Rest restores all three.
- Your abilities use the resource their description names. Ask the narrator to use one by name.
- **Gold** pays for rooms, gear and help. **Renown** changes how the keep treats you: the better known you are, the more people help you and the more they ask of you.
- Every night the barrow goes unanswered, the danger grows. Go in prepared, with light, cold iron and allies.
- Earn enough **Renown**, and Captain Blackwell trusts you with the keep's oldest secret.

## How this world is built

Emberwatch is also an example of an RPG race-and-class system. Open it in the World Editor with Advanced mode on and look at the **Traits** tab.

- **Blueprints.** The system group that holds every Race, Class and ability once. Traits under it never reach the player directly. They reach play only through links.
- **Group links.** **Wanderer**, **Albus** and **Sylvie Thornwhistle** each link the **Races**, **Classes**, **Racial Abilities** and **Class Abilities** groups. One edit to Paladin reaches every owner.
- **Trait links.** **Mother Hesk** links the **Dwarf**, **Cleric** and **Darkvision** traits. **Corvin Vale** links **Human** and **Wizard**. A single-trait link brings one original. Darkvision is default-on in Blueprints, so Hesk's link starts it on with no override.
- **Entity stats.** Hesk owns her own **Health** and **Faith**, and Corvin owns **Renown** and **Mana**. Their race and class links change their own stats, never yours: Dwarf raises Hesk's Health, and Wizard raises Corvin's Mana.
- **Per-link defaults.** Select Albus's **Classes** link and open **This Link**. Paladin is default-on there and Wizard is not. Sylvie's link makes Rogue the default.
- **Link overrides.** Select **Paladin** under Albus's **Classes** link. Its stat change is an override, so Albus gains more Faith than any other Paladin. **Reset** returns it to the blueprint.
- **Blueprint pins.** Each Class pins **Class Garb** and each Race pins **Heritage**, two placeholders in the Placeholders tab's **Blueprints** group. Each entity with a Class or a Race owns a copy of each, named like **Albus.Class Garb**, and the pin lands on that owner's copy. A copy reads the blueprint's values until you edit one. Hesk's and Corvin's copies reword the value their class and race pin, so their text reads their own words.
- **Blueprint chips.** Each Class's AI description ends with a **Class Garb** chip, and each Race's with a **Heritage** chip. A chip in a blueprint trait reads the owner's copy, so one Cleric text gives Hesk her own vestments.
- **Custom Persona.** **Wanderer** carries the Custom Persona mark, so it takes None's place at Enter World. The player enters a name, and Wanderer's links build the character. Its links also apply under a persona from your library, and its copies of **Class Garb** and **Heritage** fill in where that persona has none.
- **Persona-only.** The Custom Persona mark implies Persona-only. Unpicked, Wanderer leaves the cast and never joins a scene.
- **Same-owner gates.** **Smite** requires Paladin on the same owner. Your Wizard never unlocks it through Albus.
- **Any-of gates.** **Blessed Light** requires Cleric or Paladin. Either one unlocks it.
- **Named-scope gates.** The root trait **Squire to Albus** requires **Albus: Paladin**. Re-class Albus at Enter World and the trait locks. Play Albus and the trait is not offered, because nobody is their own squire.
- **Gated defaults and cascades.** Each racial ability is default-on and requires its race. Change race and the old ability switches off; the new one switches on.
- **Lorebook.** The **Emberwatch** book in the **Dictionary** tab holds the keep, the barrow, the broken crown and the factions, with an entry for each new place. The narrator gets an entry only when one of its keywords appears in the story.
- **Script control of lore.** **The Founders' Pact** ships off. The world script on the **Scripts** tab switches it on while your Renown is 70 or more, and off again below it.
- **World Tool.** **offer_prayer** is an On Call Tool on the stat pass. When the narration shows you pray at the Ember's brazier in the Chapel of the Ember, the AI calls it. Its script adds 10 Faith once per story day and keeps the prayer as a memory. The world still plays with Tools off.
- **Relationship labels.** Each entity's **Relationships** name who serves, rivals or owes whom. The narrator reads each one as a sentence: Albus is Corvin Vale's rival for the captain's bounty. Most ties join two people who share a place, because a tie brings its other end into every scene where either one stands.
- **Rolled label.** **Lost Sentry** in the Placeholders tab rolls the lost guard's name once per game. Mara Venn's label to the captain carries the chip, and so do her description, Sergeant Marr's and the Garrison entry, so all four read the same name.
- **Known In.** The **Cold Lights** stay among the mounds, but the narrator knows of them at the watchtower and on the wall. The **Shade of Maelis** is known nowhere until you find his vault.
- **Random presence.** **Hob Wainwright** is on the road or at the market, one of the two, picked at random each game.
- **Self openings.** Albus and Sylvie each own an opening set to **Self**. It comes up only when you play that persona, in place of the world's own openings.
- **Test Bench.** Open **Test Bench → Issues** to see the rule pass. One info finding stays by design: The Founders' Pact is off until its script switches it on.

openings.text:
The frontier road ends at the gate of Emberwatch Keep. Road dust grays {{user}}'s clothes and boots, and the gate yard beyond the arch smells of horses, tar and cold iron.

Nailed to the gate post, a call in the captain's square hand: *The barrow beyond the wall has opened. Hands wanted to go and see why. Gold and the keep's good word for those who come back with answers.*

A guard at the gate looks up from his spear. "Another one for the roll?" he asks.
I pull the captain's call off the gate post, brush the road dust from my clothes, and walk in under the arch with it in my hand. I'm here for the barrow, and I want to see whoever pays for it.

{{user}} reaches Emberwatch Keep as the sun goes down behind the ridge. The gate is half shut already. Two guards lean on it from inside, in a hurry to bar it before full dark.

Up on the wall, a bell rings once, then again. Nobody on the wall walk is near its rope.

"In or out," the older guard says, not taking his eyes off the field beyond the wall. "We close at dark now. Captain's orders."

stats.name: Health
stats.description: The body's condition. Wounds, poison and cold take it away; rest and healing return it.

descriptors.description: Dying. Barely conscious, bleeding out, one more blow from the end.
Badly wounded. Every movement costs, and fighting on is a gamble.
Hurt. Cuts and bruises, sore but able.
Hale. Whole and ready.

stats.name: Mana
stats.description: Arcane power for spells. Casting drains it; rest and study restore it.

descriptors.description: Drained. The weave slips away from every attempt to grasp it.
Low. A spell or two left before the well runs dry.
Steady. Enough power for a fight's worth of magic.
Brimming. Power hums under the skin.

stats.name: Faith
stats.description: Favor with the Ember. Prayer, mercy and courage feed it; cruelty and doubt spend it.

descriptors.description: Forsaken. Prayers fall into silence.
Shaken. The light answers slowly and dimly.
Steady. The Ember listens.
Radiant. Warmth answers before the prayer is finished.

stats.name: Gold
stats.description: Coin in the purse. Pay for rooms, gear and bribes; earn it from bounties and finds.

descriptors.description: Broke. Nothing in the purse but lint.
Scraping by. Enough for bread and a cot.
Comfortable. A good room, good gear, a round for the table.
Flush. Heavy pockets and heavier attention.

stats.name: Renown
stats.description: How widely Emberwatch knows the name. Deeds raise it; failures and cruelty lower it.

descriptors.description: Unknown. One more face on the frontier road.
Noticed. The keep's people know the name and watch what it does.
Known. Doors open; favors are asked and owed.
Famed. Songs at the Cinder and Crown, and a captain's ear on demand.

locations.name: Emberwatch Keep
locations.playerDescription: A squat stone keep at the end of the frontier road. Its gate yard smells of horses, tar and cold iron, and a call for hands is nailed to the gate post.
locations.aiDescription: The last stronghold before the wild hills, a squat square keep with a walled gate yard, stables, a smithy and a barracks. Captain Blackwell commands it. A written call for hands is nailed to the gate post: the barrow beyond the wall has opened, and the keep pays in gold and renown for anyone who will go and see why. Guards drill in the yard by day. The gate yard smells of horses, tar, woodsmoke and cold iron from the smithy. Since the barrow opened, the gate is barred at dark and the wall bell rings at every alarm.
locations.aiSummary: The frontier stronghold and gate yard where the call for hands is posted.
locations.imageTags: stone fortress, frontier keep, walled gate yard, banners, guards, overcast sky, high fantasy

locations.name: Ashford Square
locations.playerDescription: The market square of the town under the keep. Stalls, a well, a notice board and a stone plinth where a statue used to stand.
locations.aiDescription: The market square of the small town that grew up south of Emberwatch Keep, below its walls. Timber stalls sell wool, salted fish and tools. A public well stands at the center, a notice board beside it. A stone plinth marks where a statue was pulled down and never replaced. Farmers, traders and off-duty guards cross it all day; rumors travel here faster than riders.
locations.aiSummary: The town market under the keep, a well and a notice board at its center.
locations.imageTags: market street, market stalls, canvas awnings, cobblestones, small town, evening

locations.name: The Cinder and Crown
locations.playerDescription: The town's one tavern. Low beams, a fire that never goes out, and a back table where adventurers compare scars.
locations.aiDescription: A low-beamed tavern on the west side of Ashford Square, with a great hearth that has burned since the keep was raised. The taproom serves dark beer and mutton stew. A back table under the stairs belongs by custom to adventurers; maps get drawn on it in spilled beer. Rooms upstairs rent by the night. The tavern keeper hears everything and repeats half of it.
locations.aiSummary: The town tavern, its hearth and back table where adventurers gather.
locations.imageTags: medieval tavern interior, low wooden beams, great stone hearth, firelight, crowded taproom, high fantasy

locations.name: Chapel of the Ember
locations.playerDescription: A small round chapel with a brazier that is never allowed to die. Herbs hang from the rafters, and the sick lie on cots along the wall.
locations.aiDescription: A small round stone chapel on the east side of Ashford Square. A brazier at its center holds the Ember's flame, tended day and night. Bundled herbs hang from the rafters, and cots line the walls for the sick and wounded. Mother Hesk runs it as a chapel and an infirmary at once. Blessings, healing and honest counsel are found here; so is a lecture for anyone who arrives bleeding from something stupid.
locations.aiSummary: The round chapel and infirmary where Mother Hesk keeps the flame.
locations.imageTags: small round stone chapel, central brazier, sacred flame, hanging herbs, infirmary cots, warm light

locations.name: The Old Watchtower
locations.playerDescription: A cracked tower on the ridge above the keep. From its top the whole valley shows, and past the wall, the dark line of the barrow field.
locations.aiDescription: A cracked stone tower on the ridge west of Emberwatch Keep and above it, older than the keep itself. Its stair is sound but the roof is half gone. From the top the whole valley shows: the town, the river, the boundary wall, and beyond it the barrow field. The great mound's split side shows from here as a dark gash in the grass. A guard post here watches the boundary wall below, and since the barrow opened, the night watch reports cold lights moving among the mounds after dark.
locations.aiSummary: The ridge tower above the keep with a view over the wall to the barrow field.
locations.imageTags: cracked stone watchtower, broken roof, stone stairs, ridge, valley view, dusk, no humans

locations.name: The Barrow Beyond the Wall
locations.playerDescription: Past the boundary wall, a field of grassy burial mounds. One of them has opened, and cold air breathes out of it.
locations.aiDescription: A field of ancient grassy burial mounds a mile north of the keep's boundary wall. The largest mound has split open along its side where the keep quarried stone for the wall last spring, and a carved passage leads down into it. Cold air breathes out of the opening, and nothing grows near it now. Cold Lights drift among the mounds after dark. The passage leads down to the Hall of Shields, where the barrow dead guard the grave goods, and past it to the Bier Chamber.
locations.aiSummary: The opened burial mound past the boundary wall, its halls held by the barrow dead.
locations.imageTags: burial mound, grassy mound, stone doorway, field of mounds, dead grass, cold mist, gloomy sky, no humans

locations.name: The Bier Chamber
locations.playerDescription: The deepest room of the barrow. A stone bier stands under a low dome, frost on every surface, and a cold that does not come from the air.
locations.aiDescription: The round burial chamber at the heart of the great barrow, at its north end, reached down a long stair from the Hall of Shields. King Haldren's stone bier stands at its center under a low dome. Grave goods lie heaped around it: rusted arms, gold cups, and a sealed iron chest. Frost covers every surface. The Barrow Wight keeps watch here over the king it served. An empty socket in the bier's head is shaped for the crown the king was buried in.
locations.aiSummary: The frost-covered chamber at the barrow's heart, where the Wight guards the king's bier.
locations.imageTags: underground burial chamber, stone bier, low dome, frost, grave goods, dim cold light, dark fantasy

locations.name: The Boundary Wall
locations.playerDescription: The long stone wall between the town and the barrow field. Lanterns burn along its walk at night, and the sally gate below the wall bell opens onto the field.
locations.aiDescription: A wall of quarried gray stone, twice a man's height, that runs a mile across the valley floor north of the keep, between Ashford and the barrow field. The keep mended its broken stretch last spring with stone taken from the barrow field. A walk runs along its top, with the wall bell on a post above the sally gate; the bell rings at every alarm, and lately with no hand on its rope. Sergeant Ilsa Marr keeps the night watch here, two to a post. Scratches on the field side of the stone show where the barrow dead have tried the wall. The night watch lost {{ph:f8646754-94c5-584b-b55d-3e48ad468f0f:world:8752af8a-fdb1-56e0-87e0-0e01cbbe99e8}} from this walk.
locations.aiSummary: The boundary wall between the town and the barrow field, with its sally gate and its bell.
locations.imageTags: stone defensive wall, iron gate, lanterns, small gate in the wall, night, no humans

locations.name: The Smithy
locations.playerDescription: The keep's forge, hot even at midnight. Racks of new spearheads stand by the anvil, and every one of them is cold iron.
locations.aiDescription: The keep's smithy against the west wall of the gate yard: a forge, two anvils, quench barrels and racks of half-finished spearheads. Bram Oakes, the keep's smith, has worked it day and night since the barrow opened. Cold iron breaks the barrow dead, and Bram sells cold-iron blades, nails and arrowheads to anyone who will carry them past the wall. The gate yard's smell of tar and iron comes from here.
locations.aiSummary: The keep's forge, where Bram Oakes works cold iron against the dead.
locations.imageTags: medieval blacksmith forge, glowing coals, anvil, hanging tools, weapon racks, sparks, stone walls, high fantasy

locations.name: The Captain's Hall
locations.playerDescription: A long room above the gate, with a map table, a cold hearth, and an iron-bound case of old records on a high shelf.
locations.aiDescription: The captain's hall above the keep's gatehouse, east of the smithy: a long room with a map table, a cold hearth and racks of muster rolls. Captain Blackwell works here and sleeps here when he sleeps at all. The keep's founding charter and the first captains' logs sit on a high shelf in an iron-bound case. The captain keeps the key on his belt and opens the case for nobody the keep does not trust.
locations.aiSummary: The captain's hall above the gate, with the map table and the founders' records.
locations.imageTags: great hall, long map table, maps on the walls, candles, shelves, no humans

locations.name: Riverside Market
locations.playerDescription: Barges tie up at a timber quay below the town, and stalls along the bank sell what the road and the river bring. Some of it came out of the barrow.
locations.aiDescription: The river market south of Ashford Square, down the steps to the river, where barges from the lowlands tie up at a timber quay. Stalls along the bank sell rope, lamp oil, salt, wool and lowland wine. Behind the stalls, in a pawnshop with a green door, Jory Pike buys what adventurers bring up from the barrow and asks no questions. The townsfolk call barrow gold bad luck and buy it anyway.
locations.aiSummary: The river quay and its stalls below the square, where Jory Pike buys barrow finds.
locations.imageTags: riverside market, timber quay, moored barges, canvas stalls, lamp oil barrels, small pawnshop with green door, overcast, high fantasy

locations.name: The Herbwife's Cottage
locations.playerDescription: A crooked cottage at the edge of town, its garden thick with herbs. Bryony Fenn treats what the chapel can't, and asks fewer questions.
locations.aiDescription: A crooked thatched cottage on the river path at the east edge of Ashford, behind a garden of feverfew, yarrow and wolfsbane. Bryony Fenn, a hedge healer, sells salves, poultices and tonics here. Her salve cures the grave chill that a wound from the barrow dead leaves behind. She treats anyone who pays, including those who would rather Mother Hesk did not hear of it.
locations.aiSummary: The hedge healer's cottage, where Bryony Fenn cures the grave chill for coin.
locations.imageTags: cottage, exterior, herb garden, drying herbs, clay pots, riverside path, warm window light

locations.name: The Frontier Road
locations.playerDescription: The long road back toward the lowlands, rutted and lonely. A mossy waystone marks the last mile before Emberwatch.
locations.aiDescription: The frontier road runs west from the gate of Emberwatch Keep, a month's ride to the lowland towns. Its last miles cross open heath, with a mossy waystone where carters stop to water their oxen. Since the barrow opened, fewer travelers come up the road and more families go down it. Grave Hounds have been seen on the heath at dusk, and the carters now drive only by daylight.
locations.aiSummary: The road to the lowlands, with its waystone and the carts that still come.
locations.imageTags: dirt road, open heathland, mossy standing stone, rolling hills, gray sky, no humans

locations.name: The Hall of Shields
locations.playerDescription: The barrow's first great hall, lined with the rusted shields of the old king's guard. Under each shield is a burial niche, and most of them are empty.
locations.aiDescription: The first great hall below the barrow's mouth, a long vault of fitted stone. Rusted shields hang along both walls, one above each burial niche of the old king's guard, and most niches are empty now. The barrow dead stand watch here, and Grave Hounds sleep among the bones. Two ways lead on: a long stair down to the Bier Chamber, and a carved stone door to the Sorcerer's Vault.
locations.aiSummary: The barrow's hall of shields and burial niches, held by the barrow dead.
locations.imageTags: underground stone hall, arched vaults, scattered bones, skulls, torchlight, lone figure, dark fantasy

locations.name: The Sorcerer's Vault
locations.playerDescription: A side vault behind a carved stone door, its walls cut with spirals. A stone lectern stands at its center, and the air smells of old ink and thunder.
locations.aiDescription: The tomb of King Haldren's court sorcerer, a side vault east of the Hall of Shields behind a carved stone door. Spiral wards cover every wall, and the barrow dead do not cross them. A stone lectern stands at the center. The Shade of Maelis, the sorcerer's ghost, keeps the vault and holds his grimoire against his chest.
locations.aiSummary: The court sorcerer's warded tomb, where his shade keeps the grimoire.
locations.imageTags: underground crypt, spiral rune carvings, stone lectern, floating dust, faint violet glow, cobwebs, dark fantasy

entities.name: Wanderer
entities.playerDescription: You came up the frontier road with a name nobody here knows yet. You wear {{ph:2efd5460-acaf-594a-8231-f7bcf45281ac:world:a7c09709-2e76-56cd-a2de-ac68042e30a4}} and have {{ph:1a1c79e6-c73b-55db-a15e-aa0ff82a0763:world:8970f412-ae8f-5d61-ab5b-db9ebfe00b2c}}. Your race and class are yours to pick.
entities.aiDescription: {{char}} came up the frontier road alone, with a name nobody in Emberwatch knows yet. Nobody here owes {{char}} anything, and {{char}} owes nobody; every bond is still to be made.
entities.aiSummary: A newcomer to Emberwatch with no history here yet.
entities.imageTags: adventurer, traveling cloak, dusty boots, frontier road, determined, high fantasy

entities.name: Albus
entities.playerDescription: Broad and quiet, with a soldier's bearing and a patience the Ember taught. He wears {{ph:bc785559-8f16-565b-a3b7-a54f998f66b5:world:6ac3e932-5377-5fa9-9b90-4c5ccb2e2740}} and has {{ph:207bc548-27df-5a67-be79-191efe6dfda1:world:a7930ec8-b930-5ca5-bcaf-ed69487574c0}}. He came to Emberwatch because the Ember told him to, and he does not expect to leave.
entities.aiDescription: Sworn to the Ember, in his late thirties, broad-shouldered, quiet, with a scarred jaw and steady gray eyes. He speaks little and means all of it. He believes the barrow's opening is a test the Ember set for the keep, and he intends to pass it. He is protective of the weak, hard on the cruel, and slow to trust a thief. He keeps his shield polished and his oaths simple.
entities.aiSummary: The keep's quiet, steady champion of the Ember, sworn to seeing the barrow closed.
entities.imageTags: male paladin, human, late thirties, broad shoulders, scarred jaw, gray eyes, white tabard, chainmail, polished shield, sun-disc symbol

openings.text: I finish my prayer at the gate yard shrine, buckle on my shield, and go to find Captain Blackwell. The barrow has been open a month. The Ember has waited long enough.

entities.name: Sylvie Thornwhistle
entities.playerDescription: Slight, with a crooked grin and a habit of standing where the light is not. She wears {{ph:a4520beb-279c-56cb-aeb5-cc92135784c1:world:6026546d-d48c-5ec5-b62d-e3b20ec4fb9a}} and has {{ph:36d28f0c-9d34-5bb1-84f0-fe97a603c7f2:world:b247fb83-b8d3-587e-a097-98b3fe7522e6}}. She says she is here for the bounty. She is also here for the barrow's grave goods.
entities.aiDescription: Slight, quick, of indeterminate age, with a crooked grin and green eyes that miss nothing. She talks fast, lies well, and pays her debts. She answered the call for the bounty and stayed for the rumor of grave gold in the barrow. She likes Albus more than she admits and needles him constantly. She keeps a room at the Cinder and Crown and an escape route out its window.
entities.aiSummary: At the keep for the bounty and the barrow's gold, quick and quick-tongued.
entities.imageTags: female elf rogue, slight build, crooked grin, green eyes, dark leather armor, hooded half-cloak, knives, shadows

openings.text: I sit on the gate yard wall with my boots swinging and count the guards on the night watch. Then I hop down and go ask the captain how much the barrow pays, and how much of what is inside I get to keep.

relationships.label: favorite mark, whom she needles and likes more than she admits

entities.name: Mother Hesk
entities.playerDescription: The dwarf priestess who keeps the chapel flame and the infirmary cots. She wears {{ph:ab4d8e95-0627-5bce-bbcd-e00e25a6ce03:world:6172e4cd-3acd-590e-9544-53242d516de6}} and has {{ph:7f918ab1-2ae3-5f65-b4c3-a69a28275d0a:world:bedcc40f-a002-528f-8063-abe47708cd50}}. She heals anyone and scolds everyone.
entities.aiDescription: A dwarf cleric of the Ember, sixty years old and built like a forge. She runs the Chapel of the Ember as chapel and infirmary. She heals anyone who comes through her door and lectures them while she does it. She has buried three keep captains and expects to bury the fourth. She knows the barrow's old rites better than anyone alive: light to hold the dead back, cold iron to break them, and the king's crown made whole on his bier. She shares the rites with those who ask twice and show they mean to use them well.
entities.aiSummary: The dwarf cleric who keeps the chapel flame and heals the keep, blunt and kind.

He wears {{ph:ae3bc751-f4dc-5d39-bb6a-359fd448654b:world:2a11ad43-e63b-5b1b-a070-4023affcb585}} and has {{ph:1c70d45e-827c-5ce1-94b1-f101ca1bf24f:world:119b08b8-3a3c-573c-8b16-e8f3214b4aee}}. He wants the barrow's secrets for himself.
entities.aiDescription: A human wizard in his thirties, lean, well-dressed and always slightly amused. He answered the call for hands before anyone else and has bought drinks at the Cinder and Crown ever since, collecting rumors about the barrow. He believes the king's court sorcerer was buried with a grimoire, and he intends to have it before anyone else does. He is charming, competitive and capable of a quiet betrayal, but he keeps his word once it is given in front of witnesses.

entities.name: Captain Orrin Blackwell
entities.playerDescription: Commander of Emberwatch Keep. Gray at the temples, short on sleep, and shorter on patience. He posted the call and he will pay it.
entities.aiDescription: Commander of Emberwatch Keep, a career soldier in his fifties, gray at the temples and lean from worry. Last spring he had his men quarry stone from the barrow field to mend the wall, and he blames himself for what the work opened. He posted the call for hands after the night watch lost a man at the wall. He pays in gold and renown for results and has no time for heroics that bring back nothing. He trusts Mother Hesk, respects Albus, watches Sylvie and dislikes Corvin. He keeps the keep's founding records locked in his hall and opens them only for people the keep trusts. He wants the barrow closed and his people safe, in that order.
entities.aiSummary: The keep's commander, who posted the call and pays for results.

entities.name: The Barrow Wight
entities.playerDescription: The thing that woke in the barrow. A tall shape in rotted mail, eyes like two coals, and a voice that remembers the old kings.
entities.aiDescription: The risen champion of King Haldren, the last of the old kings, sworn to guard his bier past death. It is tall and gaunt, in rotted mail, and wears one half of the king's broken iron crown. Its eyes burn like coals and its voice is dry as grave dust. It thinks the keep is a trespass on the king's land, and it sends the barrow dead against the wall. Its strength grows each night it goes unchallenged. Holy light pains it, and cold iron alone cannot end it. It lies down for good when the crown rests whole on the king's bier.
entities.aiSummary: King Haldren's risen champion, who guards the bier and grows stronger each night until the crown lies whole there.
entities.imageTags: undead wight, skull face, rotted chainmail, broken iron crown, glowing ember eyes, cold mist, dark fantasy

entities.name: Wenna Tallow
entities.playerDescription: The keeper of the Cinder and Crown. Round, red-cheeked and loud, with a ladle in one hand and the town's news in the other.
entities.aiDescription: The widowed keeper of the Cinder and Crown, in her fifties, round, red-cheeked and loud. She has poured beer under the keep's walls for thirty years. She hears every rumor in Ashford and repeats half of them, and she sells the rest for a good story or a paid tab. She was a girl when the townsfolk pulled down the old king's statue in the square, and she remembers what the founders' men buried under the plinth. She feeds anyone who is hungry and throws out anyone who starts a fight.
entities.aiSummary: The Cinder and Crown's loud keeper, who trades in rumors and remembers the town's old stories.

entities.name: Barrow Dead

entities.aiDescription: The risen soldiers of the old kingdom, buried around their king. They are gray bone in rusted mail and corroded helms, with cold blue light in their eye sockets. They move slowly and stop only when broken apart. They guard the barrow's halls, and at night they come over the field to test the boundary wall. They obey the Barrow Wight. Holy light drives them back, and cold iron and blunt blows break them.
entities.aiSummary: The Wight's risen soldiers, slow and relentless, who guard the barrow and test the wall at night.

entities.aiDescription: The keep's smith, in his forties, huge and soot-blackened, with a burn scar from wrist to elbow. He has worked cold iron day and night since the barrow opened: blades, nails and arrowheads. He sells at a fair price to anyone who will take it past the wall, and at double to anyone who will not say what it is for. He served under Captain Blackwell for twenty years and would follow him into the barrow. He thinks magic is a crutch and tells every wizard so.
entities.aiSummary: The keep's smith, who forges cold iron against the dead.

She keeps the watch with lanterns, bells and one rule: nobody stands a post alone. She respects anyone who stands a watch on the wall and has no patience for anyone who will not.

Her salve cures the grave chill, the slow cold that a wound from the barrow dead leaves behind, which the chapel's prayers only slow. entries.name: Emberwatch Keep
entries.value: Emberwatch Keep holds the frontier road for the crown of the lowlands, a month's ride away. Its garrison is forty soldiers under Captain Blackwell, too few for the length of its wall. The keep has a gate yard, stables, a smithy, a barracks and the captain's hall. Since the barrow opened, the gate is barred at dark, and the bell on the wall rings at every alarm.

entries.name: The Garrison
entries.value: The garrison is loyal to Captain Blackwell and tired. The night watch lost {{ph:f8646754-94c5-584b-b55d-3e48ad468f0f:world:8752af8a-fdb1-56e0-87e0-0e01cbbe99e8}} at the wall a month ago, and nobody volunteers for it now. The soldiers fight well against living enemies and fear the dead. They respect deeds and pay little attention to talk.

entries.name: Ashford
entries.value: Ashford is the small town that grew under the keep's walls: farmers, traders, smiths and soldiers' families. Thirty years ago the townsfolk pulled down the statue of the old king that stood in the square, and its empty plinth still stands there. The old folk say the founders' men buried something under that plinth long before. The town fears the barrow and blames the keep for opening it.

entries.name: The Ember
entries.value: The Ember is the faith of the frontier: a sacred flame that is never allowed to die, and the warmth and courage it stands for. Clerics and paladins draw holy light from it through Faith. Holy light drives back the dead and pains the Barrow Wight. The Chapel of the Ember keeps its flame in Ashford, and Mother Hesk tends it.

entries.name: The Barrow
entries.value: The barrow field holds the graves of the old kingdom: a ring of small mounds around one great mound. Last spring the keep quarried stone from the field to mend its wall, and the work cracked the great mound open. A carved passage runs down from the crack through halls of grave goods to the Bier Chamber at the bottom. The barrow dead hold the upper halls. The air inside is cold enough to frost a beard, and every torch burns low.

entries.name: The Barrow Rites
entries.value: Mother Hesk knows the old rites for the restless dead. Light holds them back: the Ember's light most of all, and any honest flame a little. Cold iron and blunt blows break the lesser dead. A dead king's champion rests only when its oath is kept, so the Barrow Wight lies down for good when King Haldren's crown rests whole on his bier.

entries.name: The Broken Crown
entries.value: King Haldren was buried in an iron crown. When the keep's founders took the valley, they broke the crown in two so the old king could never rise whole. The Barrow Wight wears one half. The founders buried the other half under the statue that once stood in Ashford Square, and its plinth still marks the spot.

entries.name: The Old Kings
entries.value: Before the keep, the valley was the heart of a small kingdom of hill folk. King Haldren was its last king, and Ashford's story says he died fighting the keep's founders. He was buried in the great mound with his champion, his soldiers, his hunting hounds and his court sorcerer. The sorcerer's grimoire, a book of old death-magic, went into the tomb with them. Corvin Vale wants it.

entries.name: The Boundary Wall
entries.value: The boundary wall cuts the valley floor in two: Ashford and the keep on one side, the barrow field on the other. Forty soldiers cannot hold a mile of wall, so the night watch posts two to a lantern and rings the bell at any movement on the field. The sally gate below the bell is the only way through.

entries.name: Cold Iron
entries.value: Cold iron is iron finished on the anvil without fire. It breaks the barrow dead where steel only chips them, and nails of it driven into a threshold keep them out. Bram Oakes is the only smith in the valley who still works it.

entries.name: The River Market
entries.value: The river market is where Ashford meets the lowlands. Barges bring wine, salt and lamp oil up the river and take wool and timber down. Since the barrow opened, a quiet trade in grave goods runs through Jory Pike's pawnshop, and the old king's mark sells best of all.

entries.name: The Grave Chill
entries.value: A wound from the barrow dead does not bleed much, but it stays cold. Over days the grave chill spreads from the wound and slows the wounded until they sleep and do not wake. Prayer at the chapel slows it. Bryony Fenn's salve of wolfsbane and yarrow drives it out.

entries.name: The Frontier Road
entries.value: The frontier road is Emberwatch's only tie to the lowland towns, a month's ride away. Carts come twice a week with supplies and letters. Families have begun to leave down it since the barrow opened, and the carters will not drive it after dusk.

entries.name: The Hall of Shields
entries.value: The Hall of Shields holds the graves of King Haldren's guard, one niche and one shield for each. The guard rose as the barrow dead, and their empty niches line the hall. The hall branches to the Bier Chamber below and to the warded Sorcerer's Vault.

entries.name: The Sorcerer's Vault
entries.value: Maelis was King Haldren's court sorcerer. He swore to serve the king past death, as the champion did, and was buried in a warded vault off the Hall of Shields with his grimoire. The spiral wards keep the barrow dead out of his vault. His ghost still keeps it, and he wants his oath broken more than he wants the book.

entries.name: The Founders' Pact
entries.value: The founding charter in the captain's hall tells what Ashford has forgotten. King Haldren did not die fighting. He surrendered on the founders' oath that his people's graves would never be disturbed, and the founders killed him at the peace feast and broke his crown in two. The Barrow Wight serves a king betrayed under oath. When the keep quarried the barrow field last spring, it broke the founders' oath a second time. Captain Blackwell has read the charter and is ashamed of it.

values.text: white tabard and mail, the Ember's sun-disc bright at the throat
ink-stained blue robes and a satchel heavy with chalk and folded charts
dark oiled leathers and a hooded half-cloak, with more knives than pockets
plain gray vestments and a healer's roll of bandages at the belt
the weathered, restless look of the human frontier towns
the fine-boned grace of the elves, long ears and unhurried eyes that count years in centuries
the broad, stone-set build of the mountain dwarves, braided hair and a miner's patience
the small, quick frame of the river halflings, curly hair and a grin that opens doors

tools.name: offer_prayer
tools.description:
Purpose: Record a prayer the player makes at the Ember's brazier in the Chapel of the Ember, so the prayer raises their Faith.
Use when: The narration shows the player pray at the chapel's brazier. Call it once, before you give the stat changes.
Input: intention — what the player prays for, in a few words.
Output: A short confirmation with the new Faith. Then give the stat changes.
